definitions.explanation: Power derived from the force or movement of water, especially when used for generating electricity.

examples.japanese: {水力|すいりょく}{発電|はつでん}は{再生|さいせい}{可能|かのう}エネルギーだ。
examples.english: Hydroelectric power is a renewable energy source.

examples.japanese: ダムを{使|つか}って{水力|すいりょく}{発電|はつでん}を{行|おこな}う。
examples.english: To generate hydroelectric power using a dam.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}は{山地|さんち}が{多|おお}く{水力|すいりょく}{発電|はつでん}に{適|てき}している。
examples.english: Japan has many mountainous areas and is suitable for hydroelectric power.

notes:
COMPOSITION: {水|すい} (water) + {力|りょく} (power). Literally "water power."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{水力|すいりょく}{発電|はつでん} (hydroelectric power generation)
・{水力|すいりょく}{発電所|はつでんしょ} (hydroelectric power plant)
・{水力|すいりょく}{発電機|はつでんき} (hydroelectric generator)
・{小|しょう}{水力|すいりょく}{発電|はつでん} (small-scale hydropower)
・{揚水|ようすい}{式|しき}{発電|はつでん} (pumped-storage power generation)

TYPES OF HYDROPOWER:
・ダム{式|しき} (dam-based)
・{水路|すいろ}{式|しき} (run-of-river)
・{揚水|ようすい}{式|しき} (pumped-storage)

JAPAN CONTEXT: Japan developed many hydropower plants during the early 20th century. Famous examples include {黒部|くろべ}ダム (Kurobe Dam).

RELATED TERMS:
・{風力|ふうりょく}{発電|はつでん} (wind power generation)
・{原子力|げんしりょく}{発電|はつでん} (nuclear power generation)
・{太陽光|たいようこう}{発電|はつでん} (solar power generation)
・ダム (dam)
